A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same JustGRPO study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite the changed title and relocated analyses.

before.justification: V3 reports original decoding-order, entropy, JustGRPO benchmark, and training-efficiency results in Sections 3 and 5 and Appendices B–D.

after.justification: V4 retains original empirical results and adds baseline reproductions, random-order experiments, and general-capability evaluations in Table 2 and Appendices D–E.

M1.justification: The core JustGRPO formulation, architecture, rewards, and parallel inference remain unchanged. V4 adds the JustGRPO-Random ablation variant, using a single fixed random permutation during RL. JustGRPO-Fast corresponds to v3's existing Ours-Fast top-25%-entropy variant; its relocation and clearer explanation do not establish another method change.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds actual evaluations on MMLU, MMLU-Pro, HellaSwag, and ARC-C, substantially extending coverage from mathematics and coding to broader knowledge and commonsense capabilities. The original four reasoning benchmarks and training datasets are retained.

E2.justification: Appendix D adds fully random decoding and JustGRPO-Random as evaluated comparators. Table 1 also incorporates LLaDOU and LLaDA-1.5 into its highlighted comparison, whereas v3 explicitly excluded their displayed reference rows. The other diffusion-RL comparator identities remain unchanged, including those reproduced under aligned settings.

E3.justification: V4 adds baseline reproductions aligned on full-parameter fine-tuning, one token per decoding step, and generation length 256 (Table 2), addressing settings differences in the retained system-level comparison. It also introduces the fixed-permutation RL control and extends the HumanEval temperature evaluation from Pass@128 to Pass@256. Clarifications of existing JustGRPO settings do not establish changes to its original experiments.

E4.justification: New Appendix D tests whether random decoding avoids the confidence-based sampler's limitations and whether a fixed random training order can match left-to-right RL. It supplies sampling results, a training ablation, and a malformed-output case study. These substantively extend the alternative explanations tested. The block-size and efficiency analyses already existed in v3; the temperature analysis is extended.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The Pass@k estimator is unchanged; extending its plotted range does not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1's numerical results remain unchanged, but Tables 2 and 4–6 add substantial results. Examples include aligned GSM8K scores of 83.8/84.7/86.9 for d1/ESPO/SPG versus JustGRPO's 89.1, and 82.2 for JustGRPO-Random versus 89.1 for AR training. General-capability scores and Pass@256 temperature results are also added. Reproduced baseline scores use different settings from v3's quoted results.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 retain the same mathematical content, including the diffusion loss, Pass@k estimator, AR likelihood factorization, GRPO objective, and reward definition. V4 introduces no new theorem, proof, or substantive formal derivation.

C1.justification: V4 retains the central entropy-degradation observation and JustGRPO contribution, while narrowing categorical statements about arbitrary order to qualified findings for general mathematics and coding tasks. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion also shift from broad superiority language toward effective or competitive performance.

C2.justification: The central entropy-degradation interpretation remains. V4 adds a missing-context explanation for random-order failures, interprets general-capability retention, and frames bidirectional refinement as an expectation and future direction. It also acknowledges heterogeneous baseline settings and stronger HumanEval baselines, while removing v3's inference that length robustness rules against fixed-length memorization.

D1.justification: V4 newly specifies full-parameter tuning and one-token decoding for the retained JustGRPO results, and clarifies baseline settings and result provenance. It explains recording entropy during rollout for the existing fast variant and adds the rationale for uniformly using 125 training steps. The original hyperparameter values, hardware, data preparation, and project-page access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 adds the connection to sequence-order information through Varshney and Goyal, and cites ParallelBench and corrective diffusion models when discussing future bidirectional refinement. It removes the Dual-Token Constraints reference. Most other reference changes update publication metadata for existing works rather than introduce new research.

P1.justification: V4 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, result discussion, and conclusion, alongside the title and explanatory passages. It promotes the block-size analysis from Appendix B.3 into Section 3.1 and training efficiency from Appendix D into Section 5.3, reorganizes the appendices, and adds impact and acknowledgement sections.

P2.justification: V4 adds Tables 2 and 4–6 and revises Table 1's caption, row presentation, highlighting, and footnotes. It redraws the block-size analysis against block size, extends temperature-plot axes, and relocates the efficiency figure with renamed legends. Several other figures move or receive expanded captions while retaining their underlying graphics.

improvement.justification: V3's central performance comparison mixed fine-tuning and decoding settings without adequately exposing those differences. V4 identifies these confounds and adds aligned baseline reproductions that still favor JustGRPO, substantially strengthening the evidence for its central contribution. Random-order controls, broader capability checks, and more carefully bounded claims further improve rigor without changing the original headline results.
